Summary (short)
- Root cause: thumb-api is saturating its render worker pool and timing out requests, then returning 503s ("render rejected: no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)").
- Responsible caller: catalog-indexer — it accounts for the large majority of requests and the vast majority of 503s during the failure bursts.
- Quantified share (burst window examined):
  - Catalog-indexer = ~11,410 of 13,978 total thumb-api requests → ~81.6% of requests.
  - Catalog-indexer = ~1,314 of 1,491 total 503 responses → ~88.1% of the 503 errors.

What I inspected (time windows)
- Pod logs: last 30 minutes (09:23:00 → 09:53:00 UTC). Evidence: thumb-api pod thumb-api-58bcf947d5-lfs9m and web-frontend pod web-frontend-7f757cc945-8pnfw.
- Metrics: Prometheus queries over the same ~30m window; instant increase() queries used a 19m increase window to capture the active burst, and a 30m range query for rates.

Key evidence (selected)
- thumb-api logs (pod: thumb-api-58bcf947d5-lfs9m, many repeats):
  - 2026-10-07T09:23:26Z WARN render rejected: no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)
  - 2026-10-07T09:23:33Z WARN render rejected: no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)
  - ...repeated through the burst window
- web-frontend logs (pod: web-frontend-7f757cc945-8pnfw):
  - many lines like: 2026-10-07T09:25:27Z ERROR web-frontend thumbnail request failed: 503
  - repeated during the same intervals as thumb-api warnings
- Prometheus metric used: thumb_requests_total (labels include client, code, namespace).
  - Total requests increased during the burst (sum increase over window) = 13,978.2468
  - Per-client totals (increase over the same burst window):
    - catalog-indexer: 11,409.9938 requests
    - web-frontend: 1,383.0600 requests
    - image-proxy: 826.6219 requests
    - email-renderer: 358.5711 requests
  - 503 responses (increase over same window) total = 1,491.5353
    - catalog-indexer 503s = 1,313.7563
    - web-frontend 503s = 160.7041
    - image-proxy/email small counts

Visualization
- Thumb API request rate by client (1m rate over last 30 minutes):
<< {"type": "promql", "tool_name": "execute_prometheus_range_query", "tool_call_id": "call_eRC0oEfl8Y3YNSf9TUpc5GiA"} >>

Diagnosis (why web-frontend sees bursts of failed thumbnails)
- thumb-api has a fixed/limited render worker pool (log shows workers=4) and requests block/wait up to 1.0s before being rejected. When catalog-indexer sends large, sustained request volume, the render-workers saturate and thumb-api starts rejecting new requests with 503. web-frontend (and other callers) then surface those 503s as failed thumbnail requests.
- Catalog-indexer is the dominant source of traffic during the bursts (≈81.6% of total requests and ≈88.1% of the 503 errors), so its traffic is the primary driver of the saturation.

Concrete next actions (fast fixes)
1) Short-term (minutes)
   - Temporarily throttle/catalog-indexer requests at the caller or API gateway (rate-limit its client id) to relieve pressure.
   - Increase thumb-api replicas to spread load:
     - kubectl scale deployment thumb-api -n media --replicas=3
   - Increase worker pool in thumb-api if it's configurable via env var (example):
     - kubectl set env deployment/thumb-api -n media THUMB_RENDER_WORKERS=8
     - kubectl rollout restart deployment/thumb-api -n media
   - If you have an ingress or API gateway, add a per-client rate limit for catalog-indexer.

2) Medium-term (hours)
   - Implement per-client QoS / prioritization in thumb-api (prioritize web-frontend traffic over background jobs).
   - Add queueing/backpressure (buffer incoming work rather than immediate worker-timeout rejection).
   - Add caching or CDN for thumbnails so repeated requests don’t hit thumb-api.

3) Long-term (days)
   - Auto-scale thumb-api (HPA on CPU or custom metric like in-flight renders).
   - Instrument render queue depth and worker utilization and alert on high rejection rate (503s) or worker saturation.
   - Revisit catalog-indexer behavior: batch its requests or add back-off/retry jitter.

Suggested commands (examples you can run now)
- Scale thumb-api deployment:
  - kubectl scale deployment thumb-api -n media --replicas=3
- Increase worker env (if deployment uses env var THUMB_RENDER_WORKERS):
  - kubectl set env deployment/thumb-api -n media THUMB_RENDER_WORKERS=8
  - kubectl rollout restart deployment/thumb-api -n media
- Add temporary API gateway rate limit (example for Kong/NGINX — adapt to your gateway):
  - configure a per-client limit e.g. 100r/s for client=catalog-indexer

Confidence & caveats
- Confidence: high that worker saturation caused the 503s (log lines explicitly show "no free render worker" and 503 counts spike). Metrics clearly show catalog-indexer is the dominant request source in the burst.
- Caveat: I cannot see catalog-indexer internals (why it sent so many requests). The immediate mitigation is to throttle or batch catalog-indexer and/or enlarge/scale thumb-api. If you want, I can:
  - show a tighter time-sliced graph of 503s and requests (pick exact start/end around a particular spike),
  - fetch the catalog-indexer logs (if it's in cluster) to see what triggered the high rate,
  - or produce exact kubectl manifests/patches to change worker count if you tell me how thumb-api configures render workers (env var name or configmap).

If you want, next I can (pick one or more):
- Add a 5–10 minute plan to throttle catalog-indexer via ingress rules and scale thumb-api.
- Fetch catalog-indexer pod logs to see why it's sending bursts.
- Produce a short runbook (commands + thresholds + alerts) you can apply.
